Summary: Batch Definition & Identity Management
Description: Create and maintain the authoritative batch/section aggregate: identity, course reference, academic year/semester context. Satisfies FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, BR-01, BR-02.

Summary: Create a new draft batch
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create a new batch/section linked to a valid active course, so that a governed academic grouping exists before students can be enrolled.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am an authenticated Academic Admin with BATCH_CREATE permission, When I POST /api/v1/academics/batches with batchCode, name, courseId, curriculumId, departmentId, campusId, academicYear, semesterNo and capacity, Then a new batches document is persisted with status=DRAFT, And a BatchCreated event is written to the outbox, And the response returns batchId, batchCode, status, rosterCount and capacity per the Standard Response envelope (FR-01, UC-01, sample §29.1/29.3).

Summary: Validate courseId resolves to an active course
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to validate that courseId resolves to an active course in ACD-01 before creating or activating a batch, so that no batch can exist for an invalid or inactive course.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a courseId is supplied on create, When the service validates it against ACD-01's course reference API, Then the request succeeds only if the course exists and is active, otherwise it is rejected with 422/404 and no document is written (BR-01, Exceptions §15 'Course invalid/inactive').

Summary: Enforce batch-code uniqueness within scope
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to enforce that batchCode is unique within tenant/institution and the configured academic scope, so that duplicate batch identities can never exist.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batchCode already exists within the same tenant/institution/academic scope, When a create request is submitted with the same code, Then it is rejected with ACD_BATCH_CODE_DUPLICATE (409) and no document is written (BR-02, Exceptions §15 'Duplicate batch code').

Summary: Validate semester reference
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to validate that semesterNo/academicYear resolve to a valid semester context, so that a batch can never be created against an invalid academic period.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a semesterNo/academicYear is supplied, When the service validates it, Then invalid values are rejected with a 422 validation error (BR-01, Exceptions §15 'Semester invalid').

Summary: Update a draft or open batch
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to update the fields of a batch while it is still DRAFT or OPEN, so that I can correct or refine details before the batch becomes fully active.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch is in status=DRAFT or OPEN and I hold BATCH_EDIT permission, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/batches/{id} with changed fields, Then the fields are updated with optimistic concurrency enforced, and a BatchUpdated event is emitted (API Design §28, BR-11).

Summary: View batch detail
Description: As an authorized user (Faculty, Student, Department Head, Management), I want to retrieve the full detail of a specific batch, so that I can review its current academic context and roster status.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a valid batchId and a user with BATCH_VIEW permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/academics/batches/{id} is called, Then the current batch document is returned with HTTP 200, scoped per the RBAC matrix (UC-03, §49).

Summary: Batch Search & Catalog
Description: Provide indexed, filterable, paginated search across batches by course, year, semester, department and status. Satisfies FR-13, UC-04.

Summary: Search and filter batches
Description: As an authorized user, I want to search and filter batches by course, academic year, semester, department and status with pagination, so that I can quickly find the relevant batch in a large catalog.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/academics/batches/search or GET /api/v1/academics/batches with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then results are returned within the indexed-read performance target, and only fields appropriate to my role/classification are included (FR-13, UC-04).

Summary: Restrict batch visibility for students to their own batch
Description: As a Student, I want batch queries to return only my own/current academic batch context, so that I never see other students' batch or roster detail.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Student, When I query batch data, Then only my own current batch/section context is returned, consistent with 'BATCH_VIEW for own/current academic batch context' (RBAC §49, Actors and Personas §8).

Summary: Batch Section Management
Description: Maintain BatchSection sub-entities (sectionCode, name, capacity, optional faculty assignment) within a batch aggregate. Satisfies the diagram's Section domain entity and /sections endpoints.

Summary: Create a section within a batch
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create one or more sections within a batch, so that large cohorts can be organized into manageable groupings with their own capacity.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch exists, When I POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/sections with sectionCode, sectionName and capacity, Then a BatchSection sub-document is created within the batch aggregate, validated for a unique sectionCode within the batch (Domain Model §19, Class Model §20, sample Create Batch Request panel 8 of the diagram).

Summary: List sections for a batch
Description: As an authorized user, I want to list all sections defined within a batch, so that I can see how the cohort is organized.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch has one or more sections, When I call GET /api/v1/batches/{id}/sections, Then all section entries are returned with their capacity and status (API Design panel 3 of the diagram).

Summary: Optionally assign faculty to a section
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to optionally assign a faculty reference to a section, so that section-level faculty context is available to Timetable and HRM without ACD-04 owning faculty master data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a section exists, When I assign a facultyId to it, Then the reference is stored by identifier only, consistent with 'Assign Faculty (Optional)' (Sample Workflow panel 14) and the Boundary Rule that ACD-04 stores only logical references.

Summary: Enforce sections must have valid faculty assignment where required
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to enforce that a section has a valid faculty assignment before activation when institutional policy requires it, so that no section can go live without required staffing.
Acceptance Criteria: Given institutional policy requires faculty assignment for section activation, When a section activation is attempted without a facultyId, Then it is rejected with a 422 validation error, consistent with 'Sections must have valid faculty assignment (if required)' (Key Business Rules panel 12 of the diagram).

Summary: Capacity Management & Overrides
Description: Maintain configurable batch capacity and a governed, auditable exception store for authorized over-capacity assignments. Satisfies FR-04, FR-06, BR-03, BR-04, UC-07.

Summary: Set and update batch capacity
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to set and update the configured capacity of a batch, so that roster enrollment is bounded to a planned class size.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch exists, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/capacity with a new capacity value, Then the capacity is updated (must be positive unless zero-capacity planning drafts are explicitly permitted) and validated against the current roster count (FR-04, BR-03).

Summary: Block roster additions that would exceed capacity
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to reject adding a student to a batch when doing so would exceed its capacity, unless an authorized override exists, so that class sizes stay within policy by default.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch's current roster count equals its capacity and no active override exists, When an add-student request is submitted, Then it is rejected with ACD_BATCH_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED (409), consistent with 'Total enrolled students cannot exceed batch capacity' (Key Business Rules panel 12, BR-04, sample Error Response §29.4).

Summary: Grant an authorized capacity override
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to grant a governed, time-bound capacity override for a batch, so that legitimate over-capacity assignments are possible without bypassing policy invisibly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold CAPACITY_OVERRIDE permission with elevated approval, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/capacity-override with overrideCapacity, reason, approvedBy and effectiveFrom/To, Then a batch_capacity_overrides record is created with status=ACTIVE, a CapacityOverrideGranted event is emitted, and subsequent roster additions are permitted up to the override capacity (UC-07, Field-Level Data Dictionary §40).

Summary: Expire or revoke a capacity override
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want an expired or revoked capacity override to stop permitting over-capacity roster additions, so that the exception never silently persists beyond its intended window.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an override's effectiveTo has passed or it is explicitly revoked, When a subsequent add-student request is evaluated, Then the override's status is EXPIRED/REVOKED and standard capacity enforcement applies again (batch_capacity_overrides §40, Indexes).

Summary: Roster & Student Enrollment Management
Description: Add and remove eligible student references on the batch roster with effective-date and history support. Satisfies FR-05, FR-07, BR-05, BR-06, BR-09, UC-05, UC-06.

Summary: Add a student to a batch roster
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to add an eligible student to a batch roster, so that the student's academic grouping is authoritatively recorded for downstream timetable, attendance and examination use.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the batch is OPEN/ACTIVE and has available capacity (or an active override), When I POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/students with studentId, effectiveFrom and membershipType, Then the student's eligibility is validated via Student Management, a batch_rosters membership record is persisted, and a StudentAddedToBatch event is emitted (FR-05, UC-05, sample §29.2).

Summary: Validate student eligibility before roster assignment
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to validate that a student is active/eligible per Student Management policy before adding them to a roster, so that only eligible students can ever be enrolled.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a studentId is supplied on an add-student request, When the service resolves and validates the student through Student Management, Then the request succeeds only if the student is found and eligible, otherwise it is rejected with a 422 validation error (BR-05, Exceptions §15 'Student not found/ineligible').

Summary: Prevent duplicate active assignment to the same batch
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to reject adding a student who is already an active member of the same batch, so that roster membership stays unambiguous.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a student is already actively enrolled in the target batch, When another add-student request is submitted for the same student, Then it is rejected/treated idempotently with a 409 conflict, consistent with BR-06 and Exceptions §15 'Student already assigned'.

Summary: Remove a student from a batch roster
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to remove a student's membership from a batch roster, so that their enrollment in that batch ends while the historical record is preserved.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an active membership exists for the student in the batch, When I call DELETE /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/students/{studentId}, Then the membership status is ended (not hard-deleted), a StudentRemovedFromBatch event is emitted, and the historical membership record is retained (FR-07, UC-06, BR-09).

Summary: Block new roster additions to a closed or archived batch
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to reject any new roster addition on a CLOSED or ARCHIVED batch, so that batches that have stopped accepting membership cannot silently gain new students.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch is in status=CLOSED or ARCHIVED, When an add-student request is submitted, Then it is rejected with a 409 error, consistent with BR-07 and Exceptions §15 'Batch closed'.

Summary: Retrieve the current roster for a batch
Description: As Faculty or an Academic Admin, I want to retrieve the current roster of a batch, so that I can see who is actively enrolled.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch exists, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/roster, Then all currently active membership records are returned (API Design §28).

Summary: View point-in-time roster history
Description: As an authorized user or Auditor, I want to view the roster as it existed at a specific point in time, so that I can reconstruct historical class composition for audit or academic reporting.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch has roster membership history recorded, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/history with a point-in-time parameter, Then the roster composition as of that date is reconstructed from batch_rosters and batch_history (UC-10 View Roster History).

Summary: Batch Lifecycle Governance
Description: Govern the full batch lifecycle state machine — draft, open, active, closed, reopen, archived — without ever deleting roster or history evidence. Satisfies FR-08, BR-07, BR-12, UC-01/02/08/09.

Summary: Open/activate a draft batch
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to open and activate a draft batch, so that it becomes available to accept roster enrollment and downstream scheduling.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch is in status=DRAFT and passes validation, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/open, Then the status transitions to OPEN then ACTIVE per policy, and BatchOpened/BatchActivated events are emitted (UC-01, UC-02, Workflow §14.1).

Summary: Close a batch
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to close a batch, so that no new student membership is permitted while its roster and history remain fully intact.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch is ACTIVE and I hold closure authority, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/close, Then the status transitions to CLOSED, a BatchClosed event is emitted, new roster operations are blocked, and roster/history data is retained (FR-08, UC-08, Workflow §14.3).

Summary: Reopen a closed batch
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to reopen a closed batch where policy permits, so that roster membership can resume if the closure needs to be reversed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch is CLOSED and reopening is permitted by policy, When I call the reopen action, Then the status transitions back to ACTIVE and the transition is recorded in batch_history (UC-09, Batch Lifecycle §13).

Summary: Archive a batch
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to archive a closed batch, so that it is retained for historical records while excluded from active operational queries.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch is CLOSED, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/batches/{id}/archive, Then the status transitions to ARCHIVED, a BatchArchived event is emitted, and the record remains queryable for audit purposes (Sample Workflow panel 14 'Archive (for historical records)').

Summary: Reject invalid lifecycle transitions
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to validate every lifecycle transition against the domain state machine, so that illegal transitions (e.g. DRAFT directly to ARCHIVED) can never occur.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a requested transition is not permitted from the batch's current status per the defined state machine, When the transition action is invoked, Then the request is rejected with a 409/422 error and the batch status remains unchanged (Batch Lifecycle §13, Activity — Batch Lifecycle §26).

Summary: Batch Split & Merge
Description: Support controlled splitting of an over-enrolled batch into multiple batches and merging of under-enrolled batches, gated by Registrar approval (decided: Registrar, not Department Head, because merges can span two different departments and Registrar's authority is not department-scoped). This capability's API endpoints, events and the 'requires academic approval' rule appear only in the architecture diagram and are NOT specified in the ACD-04 Detailed Design Document — the approval AUTHORITY is now resolved, but the approval MECHANISM (routed through the College Admin Module's Approvals & Workflow capability, per ADM02) still needs to be confirmed with architecture before implementation.

Summary: Split a batch into multiple batches
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to request a split of an over-enrolled batch into two or more new batches, so that class sizes stay manageable while roster history for every affected student is preserved.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch's enrollment justifies splitting, When Academic Admin calls POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/split with the target section definitions, Then the batch enters status=PENDING_SPLIT_APPROVAL and ACD-04 publishes a BatchSplitApprovalRequested payload (envelope: eventId, eventType, eventVersion=1.0, tenantId, institutionId, correlationId, timestamp) with data: { requestId, requestType:"SPLIT", sourceBatchId, sourceBatchCode, departmentId, campusId, requestedBy, requestedAt, reason, proposedSections:[{sectionCode, capacity, targetStudentIds[]}], approverRole:"REGISTRAR" }. The split is NOT executed at this point. On later receipt of a BatchSplitApprovalDecided event with decision=APPROVED (see 'Consume approval decisions...' story), new batches are created, affected roster memberships are reassigned with full history retained on both source and new batches, and a BatchSplit event is emitted. Split does not require cross-department sign-off since source and target batches stay within the same department by default.

Summary: Merge two or more batches
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to request a merge of two or more under-enrolled batches into one, so that resources are used efficiently while every student's enrollment history is preserved, with the Registrar approving because a merge can span batches owned by different departments.
Acceptance Criteria: Given multiple batches (potentially from different departments) are eligible for merging, When Academic Admin calls POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/merge with the source batch identifiers, Then the affected batches enter status=PENDING_MERGE_APPROVAL and ACD-04 publishes a BatchMergeApprovalRequested payload (same envelope) with data: { requestId, requestType:"MERGE", sourceBatchIds[], sourceBatchDepartmentIds[] (one per source batch, needed for the cross-department check), targetBatchId (null if a new batch is created), campusId, requestedBy, requestedAt, reason, approverRole:"REGISTRAR" }. The merge is NOT executed at this point. On later receipt of a BatchMergeApprovalDecided event with decision=APPROVED, rosters are consolidated into the target batch with history retained, the source batches are closed/archived, and a BatchMerged event is emitted.

Summary: Consume ADM02's approval decision and execute or revert the split/merge
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to consume the BatchSplitApprovalDecided/BatchMergeApprovalDecided event published by the College Admin Module's workflow engine, so that the Registrar's decision — captured and audited entirely within ADM02, not via any ACD-04-owned approval endpoint — drives execution or reversal of the pending split/merge.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch is in status=PENDING_SPLIT_APPROVAL or PENDING_MERGE_APPROVAL, When ACD-04 consumes a BatchSplitApprovalDecided / BatchMergeApprovalDecided payload (same envelope) with data: { requestId, decision:"APPROVED"|"REJECTED", decidedBy, decidedAt, reason }. event matching that requestId, Then on decision=APPROVED the split/merge executes per its own story and a BatchSplitApproved/BatchMergeApproved event is emitted; on decision=REJECTED the batch reverts to its prior status, no roster changes occur, and the reason is recorded in batch_history. ACD-04 exposes NO local approve/reject endpoint of its own — the approval action itself happens inside ADM02's existing generic workflow engine (ADM02_workflow_instances), consistent with delegating approval rather than duplicating it.

Summary: Event-Driven Integration
Description: Reliably publish the batch/roster domain event catalog via a transactional outbox and consume upstream Student/Course/Curriculum/Calendar events, so ACD-01/02/05/06, EXM, LMS and Analytics stay eventually consistent. Satisfies FR-09, FR-10.

Summary: Publish domain events via transactional outbox
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want every state-changing operation to write its domain event (BatchCreated, BatchUpdated, BatchOpened, BatchActivated, StudentAddedToBatch, StudentRemovedFromBatch, CapacityOverrideGranted, BatchClosed, BatchArchived, BatchRosterChanged) to a transactional outbox in the same transaction as the business write, so events are never lost even if the broker is temporarily unavailable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch create/roster/capacity/lifecycle operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event from the Event Contracts catalog (§31) is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged (Event Architecture §30 'Batch State + Roster + History + Outbox').

Summary: Consume StudentCreated and StudentStatusChanged events
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to consume StudentCreated and StudentStatusChanged events from Student Management, so that student reference availability and roster eligibility stay current without ACD-04 becoming a shadow student master.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a StudentCreated or StudentStatusChanged event is received, When it is processed, Then a new student reference becomes available for future roster assignment, or affected memberships are flagged/blocked from future assignment respectively, without duplicating student personal master data (Event Consumption §33, Boundary Rule §3).

Summary: Consume CourseUpdated and CourseDeactivated events
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to consume CourseUpdated and CourseDeactivated events from ACD-01, so that course reference context stays current and affected batches are flagged/blocked when their course is deactivated.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a CourseUpdated or CourseDeactivated event is received for a courseId referenced by one or more batches, When the event is processed, Then course reference context is refreshed, or affected batches are flagged/blocked according to policy without deleting their history (BR-14, Event Consumption §33).

Summary: Consume CurriculumPublished and AcademicCalendarPublished events
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to consume CurriculumPublished from ACD-02 and AcademicCalendarPublished from ACD-07, so that curriculum and academic-period reference context stays current where used.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a CurriculumPublished or AcademicCalendarPublished event is received, When it is processed, Then the relevant reference context on affected batches is refreshed where used (Event Consumption §33).

Summary: Deduplicate inbound events using eventId
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to deduplicate inbound events by eventId, so that redelivered or replayed events never cause duplicate side effects.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound event with an eventId already processed successfully, When it is redelivered, Then the service recognizes the duplicate and skips reprocessing without error (Event Consumption §33).

Summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want events that repeatedly fail processing to be routed to a dead-letter queue after retries are exhausted, so that they can be investigated and replayed without blocking the main stream.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound or outbound event fails processing after the maximum configured retry attempts, When retries are exhausted, Then the event is persisted to dead_letter_events with failure context and an alert is raised (Retry Strategy §55, Monitoring §53).

Summary: Idempotency, Concurrency & Transaction Integrity
Description: Guarantee safe client retries on create/roster/capacity/lifecycle commands and correct concurrent-edit handling across batch, roster and history writes. Satisfies FR-14, §56, §57.

Summary: Support idempotent create, roster and lifecycle requests
Description: As an API client, I want to supply an idempotency key on create/add-student/remove-student/lifecycle commands, so that a retried request never creates a duplicate batch, duplicate membership or duplicate side effect.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a request is retried with the same idempotency key and identical payload, When it is reprocessed, Then the original result is returned without re-executing the write (FR-14, §56).

Summary: Reject stale writes with optimistic version locking
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want to detect when a client submits an update based on a stale batch/roster version, so that two concurrent edits can never silently overwrite each other.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a client submits an update based on a stale version, When the write is attempted, Then it is rejected with a 409 optimistic-concurrency error (BR-11, Exceptions §15 'Stale version').

Summary: Use MongoDB transactions for coupled batch/roster writes
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want batch, roster, history and outbox writes that must succeed or fail together to be wrapped in a MongoDB transaction, so that partial writes never leave the system in an inconsistent state.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a create or add-student operation touches batches, batch_rosters, batch_history and outbox_events, When the operation executes, Then all writes commit atomically or none do (Transaction Strategy §57, Workflow §14.2 step 13).

Summary: Security, RBAC & Audit Governance
Description: Enforce the full role-based access matrix (including the diagram's Parent and Accreditation Team roles), classify data sensitivity, and maintain an immutable audit trail. Satisfies FR-11, FR-12, §49-51.

Summary: Enforce the full RBAC permission matrix
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want every endpoint to check the caller's role against the RBAC matrix (Super Admin: all permissions; Academic Admin: create/edit/roster-manage/open/close; Department Head: create/edit/roster-manage within department; Registrar: approve/close/archive where authorized; Faculty: view + assigned roster view; Student: view own batch; Management: view/export where authorized; Service Accounts: scoped reference-read), so that only authorized actors can perform each action.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a user attempts an action without the corresponding permission for their role, When the request reaches the service, Then it is rejected with 401/403 per the Error Handling table (§54) before any business logic executes, and the full matrix in §49 (with its ABAC examples: tenant/institution scope match, department scope, capacity-override elevated permission) is enforced consistently across every endpoint.

Summary: Grant Parent read-only access to their child's batch and section
Description: As a Parent, I want read-only access to my child's batch and section context through the Parent Portal, so that I can view academic grouping information without any ability to modify batch or roster data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Parent linked to a specific student, When I access batch/section data via the Parent Portal, Then I receive only my linked child's current batch and section context, strictly read-only, consistent with 'View child's batch and section' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Grant the Accreditation Team read-only access to batch history and reports
Description: As an Accreditation Team member, I want read-only access to batch history and reports, so that I can verify compliance and audit trails without any ability to modify batch or roster data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as Accreditation Team, When I access batch history or reporting endpoints, Then I receive read-only results, consistent with 'View batch history and reports' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Grant External API consumers scoped read-only access
Description: As an External API consumer, I want read-only access limited to the scope defined for my API key, so that I can consume batch reference data without any write capability or over-broad visibility.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call any ACD-04 endpoint, Then I receive only the data within my granted scope and read-only access, matching 'Read-only access (as per scope)' (RBAC panel 9 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Record an immutable, append-only history entry for every material change
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want every lifecycle transition, roster change and capacity override to be recorded as an append-only entry in batch_history, so that a complete, tamper-evident audit trail always exists.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any material mutation occurs (create, update, roster add/remove, capacity override, open, close, archive), When the mutation commits, Then a corresponding batch_history record is written capturing action, actorId, timestamp and before/after context, and history records can never be updated or deleted (Audit Model §47, 'Maintain complete audit trail of all batch changes' — Key Business Rules panel 12).

Summary: Classify and protect batch data by sensitivity level
Description: As a Security Architect, I want batch data classified into L1 Public, L2 Internal, L3 Confidential and L4 Highly Restricted tiers, so that access controls and exposure match each field's sensitivity.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a field is classified L3 (membership source, notes, override approvals, audit) or L4 (outbox/idempotency/DLQ operational payloads), When a user without sufficient clearance queries batch data, Then those fields are excluded from the response (Data Classification §50). Student personal master data is never replicated into ACD-04 — only the minimum identifier needed for roster operations is stored.

Summary: Encrypt batch and roster data at rest and in transit
Description: As a Security Architect, I want all ACD-04 service communication encrypted in transit (TLS) and MongoDB data encrypted at rest, so that batch and roster data is protected against interception and storage compromise.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-04 is deployed to any environment, When traffic flows between clients, the API gateway and MongoDB, Then TLS is enforced end-to-end, encryption at rest is enabled, and no credentials or access tokens are ever stored in batch/roster documents (Encryption and Secrets §51).

Summary: Observability, Reliability & Performance
Description: Provide structured logging, metrics, tracing, alerting and defined SLOs — including roster-specific reconciliation — so operations can detect, diagnose and recover from failures quickly. Satisfies §52-55, §58-60.

Summary: Emit structured logs with correlation context
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want every ACD-04 request to emit a structured log with timestamp, service, tenantId, requestId, correlationId, actorId, operation and outcome, so that I can trace any request end-to-end across services.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any API call to ACD-04, When the request completes (success or failure), Then a structured log entry containing all required fields is emitted with no secrets/tokens present, and correlation/trace IDs propagate through asynchronous events (Logging and Observability §52).

Summary: Expose operational metrics and distributed tracing
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want request rate, latency, errors, roster operations, capacity conflicts, DB latency and event backlog exposed as metrics, plus end-to-end tracing from Gateway through ACD-04 to reference services, MongoDB/outbox, broker and consumers, so that I can monitor service health.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-04 is running in production, When metrics are scraped and traces are sampled, Then all listed metrics are available on the monitoring dashboard and a trace can be followed across the full request path (§52).

Summary: Alert on SLO-breaching and reliability signals, including roster reconciliation
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want alerts configured for API P95 >300ms, roster read P95 >500ms, elevated 5xx rate, unexpected capacity-conflict spikes, outbox backlog growth, DLQ open count, event lag and roster-count-vs-active-membership mismatch, so that incidents are caught before they impact users.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any monitored signal crosses its defined threshold, When the breach is sustained beyond the alerting window, Then an alert fires to the on-call channel with enough context to begin triage, including the roster reconciliation check (Monitoring and Alerting §53).

Summary: Apply bounded retry with exponential backoff for transient failures
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want transient failures (reference-service, broker, network) to be retried with exponential backoff and jitter up to a bounded limit, so temporary issues self-heal without manual intervention.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a transient failure occurs on a retryable operation, When the retry policy executes, Then attempts back off exponentially with jitter up to a maximum bound, and deterministic validation failures are never retried (Retry Strategy §55).

Summary: Meet indexed read/write performance targets
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want batch detail reads, search, roster reads, create/update writes and capacity-override writes to meet their defined P95 latency targets via proper indexing, so the service remains responsive at institutional scale.
Acceptance Criteria: Given production-representative load, When each workload type is exercised, Then API P95 stays within the documented threshold and roster reads P95 stay under the documented target, verified in performance testing (Performance §60, MongoDB Index Strategy §44).

Summary: Validate disaster recovery via regular restore tests
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want automated MongoDB backups with tested restore procedures, so that ACD-04 can meet its defined RPO/RTO in a disaster scenario.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the configured backup schedule, When a scheduled restore test is executed against a non-production environment, Then the restored dataset is verified complete and consistent, including roster membership integrity (Disaster Recovery and Backup §58).

Summary: API Standards, Error Handling & Contracts
Description: Deliver a consistent, versioned REST contract with standardized request/response envelopes and the full documented error taxonomy across all ACD-04 endpoints. Cross-cutting.

Summary: Publish and version the ACD-04 API contract
Description: As an API Consumer, I want a versioned specification covering every /api/v1/academics/batches endpoint (create, list/search, detail, update, roster get/add/remove, open, close, archive, capacity update, capacity-override, history), so that I can integrate against a stable, documented contract.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-04 service, When the API contract is published, Then it documents every endpoint in the REST API Specification (§28) with request/response schemas, and breaking changes require a new API version.

Summary: Return standardized success and error envelopes
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every response to follow the standard {success, data, meta} / {success:false, error, meta} envelope with requestId and correlationId, so that clients can handle responses uniformly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any ACD-04 API call, When the response is returned, Then it conforms to the Standard Response / Error Response shapes in §29.3/29.4.

Summary: Map every documented failure family to its specified HTTP status
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every failure family (malformed request, authentication, authorization, not found, conflict, business validation, rate limit, internal error, dependency unavailable) mapped to its documented HTTP status, so that I can build reliable client-side error handling.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each documented failure condition occurs, When the API responds, Then it returns exactly the status defined in the Error Handling table (§54): 400 malformed, 401 authentication, 403 authorization, 404 not found, 409 conflict (duplicate/student-already-assigned/stale-version/capacity), 422 validation (course/semester/eligibility), 429 rate limit, 500 internal, 503 dependency unavailable.

Summary: End-to-End Scenarios & Cross-Module Integration
Description: Validate complete cross-cutting flows spanning creation, sectioning, roster enrollment, capacity handling and every listed downstream module integration (ACD-01/02/03/05/06, STM, HRM, EXM, COM, ACD-10). Satisfies Testing Strategy §68 and Cross-Module Integration panel 11.

Summary: E2E: Create → Sections → Faculty (optional) → Activate → Enroll → Monitor Capacity
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test that follows the full sample workflow (Create Batch Draft, Define Sections & Capacity, Assign Faculty Optional, Activate Batch, Enroll Students, Monitor Capacity, Update Batch Details), so that the complete authoritative-batch lifecycle is proven to work together exactly as designed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a fresh batch is created via UC-01, When it proceeds through section definition, optional faculty assignment, activation and student enrollment, Then roster count and capacity are consistent at every step and the resulting events (BatchCreated, BatchActivated, StudentAddedToBatch) are observed, verified end-to-end (Sample Workflow panel 14 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: E2E: capacity override enables enrollment beyond default capacity, then expires
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test proving that a batch at full capacity rejects new enrollment, an authorized override then permits it, and after the override expires enforcement reverts to default capacity, so BR-04 and the override lifecycle are continuously verified.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch is at its configured capacity, When an add-student is rejected, a capacity override is granted, the add-student then succeeds, and the override subsequently expires, Then a further add-student attempt beyond the original capacity is rejected again, verified end-to-end.

Summary: E2E: batch closure blocks new enrollment while preserving roster history
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test that closes an active batch and verifies new enrollment is blocked while existing roster and history remain fully intact and queryable, so BR-07/BR-08/BR-09 are continuously verified.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an ACTIVE batch with existing roster members, When Workflow §14.3 (Close Batch) is executed end-to-end, Then the batch status becomes CLOSED, a further add-student attempt is rejected with 409, and all prior roster/history entries remain intact and queryable (Workflow §14.3, BR-07/08/09).

Summary: Validate integrations with ACD-01, ACD-02, ACD-03, ACD-05, ACD-06, STM, HRM, EXM, COM and ACD-10 before production sign-off
Description: As a Release Manager, I want end-to-end integration tests against every module listed in the Cross-Module Integration table executed as part of the Production Definition of Done, so that ACD-04 is not released until its downstream contracts are proven.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-04 release candidate, When the full integration suite runs against ACD-01 (validate course & program), ACD-02 (validate semester structure), ACD-03 (ensure subject availability), ACD-05 (allocate timetable slots), STM (student enrollment & validation), HRM (faculty assignment), EXM (batch-wise exam scheduling), COM (notify batch-related updates) and ACD-10 (batch analytics & reports), Then all contract, event-schema and E2E scenarios pass, and this gate is required before the service is marked production-ready (Production Definition of Done §69, Cross-Module Integration panel 11).

Summary: Define BATCH_SPLIT_APPROVE / BATCH_MERGE_APPROVE permission codes and grant them to Registrar
Description: As a Platform/Identity Administrator, I want dedicated BATCH_SPLIT_APPROVE and BATCH_MERGE_APPROVE permission codes defined and granted exclusively to the Registrar role, so that split/merge approval authority is explicit, auditable and not accidentally inherited by Academic Admin or Department Head.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the new permission codes are registered in the platform's central role→permission catalog (owned by the College Admin Module's Identity/Role & Access capability, not by ACD-04 itself), When the Registrar role is provisioned, Then BATCH_SPLIT_APPROVE and BATCH_MERGE_APPROVE are included in its grant set by default, and no other role (including Academic Admin and Department Head) holds either permission unless a future explicit decision changes this. This decision (Registrar, not Department Head, chosen specifically because merges can span batches from more than one department and Registrar's authority is not department-scoped) is not documented in either the ACD-04 DDD or the architecture diagram and should be captured in both.

Summary: Define BATCH_SPLIT_REQUEST permission for Academic Admin
Description: As the Batch Management Service, I want a BATCH_SPLIT_REQUEST permission code separate from the approval permission, so that Academic Admin can initiate a split/merge request without being able to self-approve it.
Acceptance Criteria: Given Academic Admin holds BATCH_SPLIT_REQUEST but not BATCH_SPLIT_APPROVE/BATCH_MERGE_APPROVE, When they call the split or merge endpoint, Then the request-initiation succeeds and enters a pending-approval state, but any attempt by that same actor to call the approve/reject endpoint on their own request is rejected with 403, enforcing separation of duties between requester and approver.

Summary: Carry a full roster-reassignment map in BatchSplit/BatchMerged events for downstream reconciliation
Description: As a downstream consumer (ACD-05 Timetable, STM Student Management, HRM Faculty, EXM Examination, ACD-10 Reporting), I want the BatchSplit and BatchMerged events to include an explicit old-batchId/student-to-new-batchId reassignment map (not just the new batch identities), so that every module holding its own batch-scoped state (timetable slots, student enrollment records, faculty assignments, exam schedules, analytics lineage) can reconcile independently without querying ACD-04 or guessing at the mapping.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a split or merge executes after Registrar approval, When the BatchSplit or BatchMerged event is published, Then its payload includes: sourceBatchId(s), resultingBatchId(s), and a per-student array mapping each affected studentId from its old batchId/sectionId to its new batchId/sectionId. Given this event schema, When ACD-05, STM, HRM, EXM or ACD-10 consume it, Then each can update its own batch-scoped records without a follow-up query to ACD-04. NOTE: this story defines what ACD-04 must publish; it does NOT define how ACD-05/STM/HRM/EXM/ACD-10 consume and apply it — those are gaps in THEIR respective DDDs (none of which were available when this backlog was built) and should be raised as action items with each module's owning team before batch split/merge ships.
